verdict: Broad chip selloff Oct 9 (NVDA -3%, AVGO -4.4%, MU -4.8%) on 10yr yield spike to 5.36%; DRAM pricing decelerating but supply tight through 2027; USITC solar AD/CVD injury vote Oct 14 is next week's scheduled catalyst.
body_md:
## Fresh developments (last 24–72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM pricing:** TrendForce Sep 30 release: Q4 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices +10–15% QoQ — marked deceleration from Q1's +90–95% spike. PC DRAM +13–18% QoQ. NAND +15–20% QoQ. HBM3E 2026 annual contracts ~+20% YoY. Memory supply tight through 2027; blended HBM ASP forecast +121% YoY for 2027.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 ramp:** SK Hynix slipped HBM4 ramp from Q2→Q3 2026 due to sustained HBM3E demand occupying existing capacity. Samsung targeting ~250K wafers/month HBM by YE 2026 (+47% vs current 170K). SK Hynix filed F-1/424B4 SEC forms — potential equity offering. Late-2026 capacity build is happening per baseline correction-risk scenario.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler capex:** No fresh guide-down. 2026 aggregate trackers now read $720–745B (above baseline $600–700B). Meta raised guidance to $125–145B (from $115–135B). No October surprises.

**Signal 4 — AMD/Custom ASIC:** No breaking Oct 2026 news. SemiAnalysis unconfirmed report: Google reportedly engaging AMD for next-gen (v10) TPU hybrid ASIC with on-package CPU cores. AMD Helios rack (72× MI455X, 31TB HBM4) on track for YE 2026.

**Signal 5 — Optical/photonics:** Marvell (MRVL) exhibiting open AI infrastructure at OCP Global Summit this week — potential near-term catalyst. Lumentum (LITE) won a large ultra-high-power laser procurement order worth hundreds of millions; shipments H1 2027. No fresh CIEN news.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Section 232 tariff: 15% on polysilicon + derivatives proclaimed Aug 6; minimum import prices (poly $21/kg, modules $0.38/W) effective Dec 4. **Key imminent catalyst: USITC injury vote on India/Indonesia/Laos AD/CVD October 14** — outcome directly affects FSLR, ARRY, NXT. US solar panel inventories elevated; utility-scale project starts slowing.

## Context vs baseline

DRAM rate-of-change is peaking: still rising (+10–15% QoQ) but nowhere near Q1's +90–95%. SK Hynix slipping its own HBM4 ramp while Samsung adds 47% HBM capacity confirms the correction-risk scenario is building on schedule. Hyperscaler capex tracking above baseline ($720–745B vs $600–700B) — no demand cliff yet. Oct 9 chip selloff is macro/rates-driven (10yr at 5.36%), not a fundamental break; demand signals intact. HIVE's BUZZ HPC $350M deal (Aug) shows GPU cloud demand real but the stock is crypto-correlated and dilution-prone — watch Q4 go-live execution.

## Most important development

Friday's broad chip selloff (NVDA −3%, AVGO −4.4%, MU −4.8%, AMD −3.9%, MRVL −3.5%) on the 10-year Treasury spiking to 5.36% is the most immediately actionable event — macro-rate rotation, not a fundamental break. The **Oct 14 USITC injury vote** on India/Indonesia/Laos solar panels is the next scheduled hard catalyst for FSLR/ARRY/NXT. On the memory cycle, DRAM pricing deceleration + Samsung HBM capacity surge are the clearest structural data points confirming the 2027 correction-risk signal from baseline.
